unit.why: A short anecdote about the Maggid of Mezritch: he insists in prayer for a sick man, Heaven tells him he has lost his share in the World to Come, and he resolves to pray for Israel without hope of reward.
unit.boundary_note: The trailing heading 'מענין התגלות' belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: ע״ד המעשה המובא בשם אדמו״ר איש אלהים
stories.summary_en: The Maggid of Mezritch persists in prayer for a sick man until he is healed; Heaven informs him that he has lost his share in the World to Come for this, and after his first alarm he resolves that he can now pray for Israel truly, without any thought of reward.

הנה עתה העת להתפלל עבור ישראל
tags.why: The story is about insistent prayer.

quotes: ולא רצה לנטות מעליו עד יתרפא
tags.why: He prays for the healing of a sick man.

quotes: והודיעו לו מן השמים כי אבד חלקו בעוה״ב

tags.why: He is alarmed by the heavenly decree.
The loss of his share in the World to Come is central.
The story illustrates the tzaddik's selfless devotion and his service without reward.

tags.why: Disinterested service is the virtue at issue.
